newsitem.title: USA: Two killed in Nashville dynamite blast.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in Nashville dynamite blast.

text.p: An explosion at a construction site near downtown Nashville killed at least two workers on Monday and shut down two interstate higways, backing up traffic for miles.

Fourteen people, including 12 motorists, were taken to hospitals with injuries. Police spokesman Don Aaron said two construction workers had been confirmed killed in the blast, their bodies blown into oncoming traffic.
"A premature explosion at a construction site occurred on the bluff overlooking the juncture of Interstate 40 with Interstate 24, resulting in total traffic gridlock," Aaron said.
The blast occurred during the morning rush-hour at a project to widen exit ramps.

Dazed motorists screeched to a halt as debris rained over them, shattering car windscreens. At least one vehicle was struck by a body that had been hurled onto the highway. Other drivers rammed into the cars ahead of them.
Aaron said the injuries to the 12 motorists and two construction workers were apparently not life-threatening, and that everyone at the site had been accounted for.
The explosion blew out windows at a motel and coffee cups were tossed off counters at a nearby coffee house.
Early reports said witnesses heard two blasts, but this was not confirmed by officials.
Police were able to reopen one lane of traffic heading into the city on Interstate 24 about 90 minutes after the explosion.
